items.doc: David N. Baker SI-NEA oral history (2)
items.title: David N. Baker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Sam Floyd sent me a copy of the video... I think, again, we respond to time and place. ... places such as the center which Sam Floyd runs.

ctx.x: I know at one point you were approached about writing an opera based on the life of Malcolm X. Then at one point, too, a project was proposed to you which I found very interesting, the project called The Meeting.

We talked earlier about the Malcolm project. I didn’t do that simply because it would have made an encroachment on my time that I was unwilling to give. The Meeting was a little more impressive to me. Sam Floyd sent me a copy of the video that was a mythical meeting between Malcolm X and Martin Luther King. It was going to be a two-man play. They talked about their differences, but their commonalties. I was approached, and I found that very exciting, to write an opera, a two-person opera based on that. I have no…

I know you have a great affection for Dr. King, and you’ve studied his writings and you’ve studied his life. And also, the life of Malcolm X has been something of great interest to you. Would you speak a little bit about them and possibly Medgar Evers and others of the pioneers in the civil rights movement that have affected you personally?
